extracted.intended_audience: physicians, sanitary reformers, and public-health-minded medical professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Normative guidance for physicians about their future role emphasizing preventive medicine, sanitary instruction, holistic understanding of patients (moral and physical), and public education—including the special role of women in household sanitary instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority of preventive medicine over curative work
rubrics_metrics.description: Preventive measures are better than curative; it is a nobler and higher task to prevent disease than to heal it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The physician's future work should largely be teaching people how to live so that they may avoid disease. He may often be more certain of his position as a preventer than as a healer; prevention can produce more beneficent results than the greatest triumphs of cure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physician's responsibility for moral as well as physical well-being
rubrics_metrics.description: The physician is to seek to make men better morally as well as physically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because health influences moral judgment and behavior, sanitary instruction and prevention undertaken by physicians will also lessen crime and improve moral character. Physicians should hold before their minds the goal of improving both the physical and moral condition of individuals and communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holistic understanding of the patient (mind and body)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before he can influence the moral as well as the physical nature of man the physician must understand what man is — his feelings, emotions, thoughts, as well as the course of the blood and the action of organs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anatomists and physiologists must avoid treating the body as the whole of man; knowledge of the patient's inner life (the 'higher part' or soul) is necessary to appeal effectively and achieve full development of both physician and patient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educate and empower women in sanitary instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Women, more than men, regulate the condition of the home and therefore should have a thorough medical education so they may instruct other women and girls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because women bear children and manage food, clothing, and general training, they are central agents for sanitary education; physicians should ensure women receive sufficient medical training to communicate what is necessary to households.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physician as public educator and sanitary reformer
rubrics_metrics.description: Physicians have unique opportunities to disseminate sanitary knowledge and apply it in everyday life, thereby improving the race (longer-lived, more vigorous, happier, and better).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The dissemination and practical application of sanitary knowledge by physicians can produce generational improvements; physicians should seize leadership in sanitary movements or risk losing that role to others less suited to it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance research for remedies with public-health duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The search for remedies and cures is noble but should not displace the greater task of sanitary instruction and prevention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While giving time and strength to discovering means to heal or alleviate, physicians must not let that work supplant sanitary education and prevention, which are described as a far grander task.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous intellectual humility and effort to reduce 'blindness' in practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Physicians should be ready to exert themselves to open their eyes as far as possible — to be as little blind and as seldom as may be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Human skill and knowledge often reach limits before disease does; physicians must continually seek knowledge to prevent disease they cannot cure and strive to recognize the limits of their understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize interplay between physical disease and moral/legal responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical disorder (sickness, pain, morbid bodily conditions) may lie at the foundation of much that we call crime; therefore physicians and society should consider disease's role when judging actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although crime must be punished, doubt about its causal relation to disease permits charity and leniency in judgment when consistent with societal welfare. Analogously, insanity exempts moral responsibility; other morbid conditions may similarly dwarf moral instincts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to patients' higher beliefs (soul/future) to motivate sanitary behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: If a man can be brought to understand that his present life affects his future (and that the body as medium affects the soul), he will be more ready to listen to teachings that improve physical and spiritual life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Belief in capacity for growth and progress, and in a 'soul' that is affected by bodily condition, can be used by physicians and sanitary reformers as sustaining truths to motivate individuals toward better living and adoption of preventive practices.
